name: canonical-json-rfc8785
description: Canonical JSON is RFC 8785 (JCS). These are the cases where a naive implementation silently disagrees, which matters because the plaintext under end-to-end encryption is canonical JSON (§7.1, §8.1): a one-byte difference produces ciphertext the other side cannot authenticate.

cases.description: RFC 8785 section 3.2.3, the specification's own vector

Keys sort by UTF-16 code unit. U+1F600 is a surrogate pair whose first unit is 0xD83D, so it sorts BEFORE U+FF00 even though its code point is higher. Code-point or UTF-8 byte ordering gets this backwards.
Uppercase sorts before lowercase; ordering is over code units, not a locale collation
Integer-like keys get no special treatment; they sort as strings, so "10" precedes "2"
Negative zero serializes as 0. Safe to run even where the vector file's own parser folds -0 to 0, since the expected output is the same either way.
Exponent form is used at and above 1e21, and at or below 1e-7, per ECMAScript Number::toString
Trailing zeros are dropped and the shortest round-tripping form is used
Largest exactly representable integer keeps integer form
Short escapes are preferred where they exist; other control characters use lowercase \u00XX
Non-ASCII is emitted raw as UTF-8, never escaped
Quote and backslash are escaped; forward slash is not
Nesting is canonicalized recursively; array order is data and is never sorted
